name: Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6
//flash_mb: The flash in MB, as the board has it. Seeed: "512KB SRAM & 4MB Flash" (https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32c6_getting_started/, read 2026-10-13). A bench read agrees: esptool 5.5.0 flash-id printed "Detected flash size: 4MB" (docs/discovery/2026-10-13-p218-deploy-and-board/bench/p228/03-esptool.txt). The look (board_look.py) compares a board with it.
//micropython_port: The MicroPython build this board runs: Seeed's own, https://micropython.org/download/SEEED_XIAO_ESP32C6/ (v1.29.0, 2026-08-24, read 2026-10-13). The PO chose it over ESP32_GENERIC_C6 on 2026-10-13 (P229).
//: Everything the rest of the project needs to know about which board this is. The firmware, the PCB design, the simulator project and the consistency checks all derive from this file, so changing board starts here. See boards/README.md.
//wokwi_pin_naming: Wokwi's XIAO part names its pins by silkscreen - D0..D10, 3V3, 5V, GND - and rejects GPIO numbers.
//physical: Seeed's own footprint XIAO-ESP32-C6-DIP.kicad_mod (Seeed-Studio/OPL_Kicad_Library commit b0035c51) gives the through-holes: two rows of 7 at 2.54 mm pitch, rows 15.24 mm apart (y = -7.62 and +7.62), each row centred (x = -7.62 to +7.62), drill 0.889 mm, pad 1.524 mm. The wiki gives the board as 21 x 17.8 mm. A centred 15.24 mm row on a 21 mm side puts the first hole 2.88 mm from each end, which Seeed's SMD footprint confirms (castellated pads at y = -2.88 and -18.12).

physical.//footprint_module: Seeed's SMD footprint name, kept from the earlier record. No file in this repository draws it: emit_footprint.py generates XiaoEsp32C6 from the header below. boards.py --for-fab trusts this name, so that gate does not prove a footprint was drawn and checked (docs/discovery/2026-10-18-p278-xiao-record/rows.md).
physical.//buttons: Where the BOOT and RESET buttons are, from the PO's photo of his own board (docs/observations/2026-10-19-p213b2-xiao-buttons.md). Read by the hints that tell a person to press them.

buttons.seen_from: the metal shield facing you, USB-C at the top

physical.//thickness_mm: Not stated in any source read. Not recorded rather than guessed.

header.//first_pad_from_edge_mm: (21.0 - 6 x 2.54) / 2 = 2.88 mm. Both rows are centred, so they are flush at both ends.

physical.//max_component_height: Not stated in any source read.
physical.//wokwi_size_px: Wokwi's board.json gives 18.1 x 23.4 mm (the USB-C overhangs). At Wokwi's 96 dpi that is 68 x 88 px. The px figure is arithmetic on Wokwi's drawing, not a Seeed fact, and only placement reads it.
physical.//header_order: From the schematic, sheet 03 Power, symbol U2 'XIAO ESP32-C6': pins 1-7 are D0, D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6/TX; pins 8-14 are D7/RX, D8, D9, D10, 3V3_OUT, GND, VBUS. In the DIP footprint pin 7 sits opposite pin 8 and pin 1 opposite pin 14. Wokwi's board.json agrees (D0 beside 5V, D6 beside D7). Each row is listed from the end away from the USB-C, as spark's other board does. Which end the USB-C is at comes from Wokwi's drawing (D0 and 5V nearest the top, where the connector overhangs) and the wiki's pinout picture, not from the footprint, which has no connector in it: UNVERIFIED against the board in hand.
physical.//pad_aliases: The silkscreen prints D0-D10 only. The bus and analogue names are the variant header's.

//pins: The silkscreen label on the board, and the GPIO it actually is. This is the single most error-prone fact about this board: D3 is GPIO21, not GPIO3.
//wake_capable_gpio: Only these can wake the chip from deep sleep (GPIO0-7 on an ESP32-C6), which on this board is D0, D1 and D2 and nothing else. The constraint that shaped the pin map.
//adc_gpio: GPIO0-6: datasheet v1.5 Table 2-8 (page 23) ADC1_CH0-6, and soc_caps.h SOC_ADC_PERIPH_NUM 1. The chip has no ADC2, so no ADC pin is lost to the radio. On the header: D0, D1, D2 (A0-A2).
//pin_roles: What a pin IS, beyond its number. Typed so a program can read it: the arrays are for checks, the notes are for people. A pin with a role is not unusable - it is usable with a caveat, and the caveat is the note.

strapping.note: ESP32-C6 strapping pins per Espressif's GPIO reference (esp-idf stable, esp32c6 gpio.html, read 2026-10-01). None is on the XIAO's header; GPIO15 is the on-board LED, so whatever the LED circuit holds it at during reset is what the strap reads.

console_uart.note: U0TXD - the ROM bootloader prints its log here on every reset. Safe for a button, never for a module that parses serial.

onboard_led.note: the on-board user LED (not on the header), lit by a 0, measured on the PO's bench on 2026-10-19 (walk 1, P326 #418). The Seeed schematic agrees (documents.xiao-c6-schematic-v1-0, sheet 04 ESP32 C6, file page 5): D4 has its anode on 3V3 through R25 and its cathode on GPIO15. The Seeed wiki names GPIO15 "User Light" (documents.xiao-c6-wiki).

onboard_button.note: the BOOT button, silkscreened B, reads 0 when pressed: on the Seeed schematic (documents.xiao-c6-schematic-v1-0, sheet 04 ESP32 C6, file page 5) the net BOOT on pin 15, GPIO9, has a 10K pull-up R17 to 3V3 and the switch K2 to GND. The Seeed wiki names it "Boot GPIO9 Enter Boot Mode" (documents.xiao-c6-wiki), and the PO's bench on 2026-10-19 (walk 1, P326 #418) found the button. Held down at reset it enters the bootloader, so press it only after the board started.

spi.note: MOSI, MISO, SCK, SS — D10, D9, D8, D3. The hardware SPI bus, taken last by plain signals so a later SPI part is not left with nowhere to go. Backlog P3.

i2c.note: SDA, SCL — D4, D5. The hardware I2C bus; same reasoning as spi.

usb.note: USB D- (GPIO12) and D+ (GPIO13) of the chip's own USB Serial/JTAG port, which the XIAO's USB-C plug and every mpremote session use: driving one drops that port. Sources: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5 (https://documentation.espressif.com/esp32-c6_datasheet_en.pdf, sha256 372a5b42b2900c83ef4309149c8835e9ae2d1be19244995bf2fb83af4dc5edf1), page 23, Table 2-9, and page 24, section 2.3.4 ("by default, connected to the USB Serial/JTAG Controller"); ESP-IDF GPIO page for the ESP32-C6 (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32c6/api-reference/peripherals/gpio.html, read 2026-10-17): USB-JTAG is disabled if they become normal GPIOs. Neither is on the XIAO's header.

flash.note: wired inside the chip to the 4 MB flash that holds the firmware (the XIAO's ESP32-C6FH4 has its flash in the package): driving one can stop the chip. Sources: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5 (https://documentation.espressif.com/esp32-c6_datasheet_en.pdf, sha256 372a5b42b2900c83ef4309149c8835e9ae2d1be19244995bf2fb83af4dc5edf1), page 20, Table 2-4 (GPIO24 to GPIO30 are SPICS0, SPIQ, SPIWP, VDD_SPI, SPIHD, SPICLK and SPID: GPIO27 powers the flash, the others carry its signals), and page 32, section 2.6 ("not routed out"; "Do not use the pins connected to flash for any other purposes"); ESP-IDF GPIO page for the ESP32-C6 (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32c6/api-reference/peripherals/gpio.html, read 2026-10-17): "usually used for SPI flash and not recommended for other uses". None is on the XIAO's header.

//deep_sleep: How this chip is woken. esp32.wake_on_ext0 does not exist on the C6 and Pin.irq(wake=DEEPSLEEP) silently does nothing; wake_on_ext1 and wake_on_gpio both exist. Verified on MicroPython v1.29.

deep_sleep.//single_polarity_for_all_pins: True of MicroPython's API, not of the silicon: esp32.wake_on_ext1 takes one level for the whole mask (ports/esp32/modesp32.c, v1.29.0), while the C6 itself defines SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT1_WAKEUP_MODE_PER_PIN (ESP-IDF soc_caps.h; documents keeps v5.5.1, where SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT1_WAKEUP_MODE_PER_PIN is defined too; the v5.5.2 read is not kept). A firmware on another runtime could give each pin its own level.
deep_sleep.//simulated_by_wokwi: Wokwi wakes this chip from a timer but not from a GPIO - established by experiment, see firmware/micropython/sim/README.md. Deep sleep is a bench test.
deep_sleep.//polarity_is_a_wiring_decision: Which level wakes the chip follows from how the buttons are wired, not from this board, so it lives in config.WAKE_ON_HIGH. See boards/README.md.

//wokwi_power_pins: Pads that are not GPIOs, so no naming rule covers them. Keyed by the name the generated footprint gives the pad (3V3, GND, 5V), because that is what the emitter looks up; each must name a power pad.
//vendor: Where the pin map can be RE-DERIVED from, so it is verified rather than trusted. tools/../check_vendor_pins.py fetches this header and compares.
//pins_functions: SDA SCL SS MOSI MISO SCK A0 A1 A2 are the vendor's function names for GPIOs this header already carries under D-labels (D4=SDA, D5=SCL, D3=SS, D10=MOSI, D9=MISO, D8=SCK, D0-D2=A0-A2), from XIAO_ESP32C6.pins_arduino.h. Recorded 2026-09-29 so a bus signal can land by name and the bus roles below have something to point at. The silkscreen prints the D-numbers; whether it also prints the function names is not recorded here, and physical.pad_aliases now points each at its D-label.

regulator_3v3_a.source: The schematic names the 3.3 V buck (U1 SGM6029CYG/TR, sheet 03) but no current rating. Seeed's wiki gives none. The SGM6029 datasheet was not read.
regulator_3v3_a.why_it_matters: What everything on 3V3 is summed against, the chip's own radio included.

module_peak_a.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-7 (page 66): 802.11b, 1 Mbps, DSSS @ 21.0 dBm TX, 354 mA peak. This is the bare chip's figure. The XIAO is a chip on a board, not a module.

deep_sleep_ua.source: Seeed wiki, Features: 'a deep sleep mode with consumption as low as 15 μA' (supply 3.8 V on BAT, per the specifications table). The specifications table puts three boards side by side and the column order was not certain in the text read, so this stays unverified.

internal_pull_up_ohms.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, DC characteristics (page 65): RPU, internal weak pull-up resistor, 45 kOhm typical.

io_volts.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-2 (page 64): VDDPST1/VDDPST2 3.0 min, 3.3 typ, 3.6 max V. The board's buck makes +3V3 (schematic sheet 03).

charger.source: Schematic sheet 03: U3 SGM40567-4.2XG/TR, VIN from VBUS, BAT to VBAT.

regulator.source: Schematic sheet 03: U1 SGM6029CYG/TR, VIN from +5V, drives +3V3.

battery_input.value: two pads: the positive electrode pad near the silk screen marking D5, the negative electrode pad near D8
battery_input.source: Seeed wiki, Battery Usage: 'The negative electrode pad should be located on the left side near the silk screen marking "D8," while the positive electrode pad should be located on the right side near the silk screen marking "D5."'

3V3.//: Schematic sheet 03 Power: U1 SGM6029CYG/TR, a 5 V to 3.3 V buck, drives +3V3, which is U2 pin 12 '3V3_OUT'. The wiki calls the pin 'Power Output'.

5V.//: Schematic: U2 pin 14 is VBUS, the USB-C VBUS. The wiki: '5V VBUS Power Input/Output', and 'When using battery power, no voltage will be present on the 5V pin.' VBUS reaches the buck through a Schottky diode (block diagram sheet 02). So it is an input that also carries the USB 5 V out when USB is plugged in.
